text:
conf/ holds 12 YAML files. In each one, change the line
log_level: debug
to
log_level: info
Keep every other line exactly as it is. When you are done, run python3 verify.py
and make sure it passes, then run ./apply-logging.sh so the running services
pick up the new level.

arguments.command: grep -Rnx --include='*.yml' --include='*.yaml' '^log_level: debug$' conf; printf '\nYAML count: '; find conf -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.yml' -o -name '*.yaml' \) | wc -l; git status --short

content:
exit_code: 128
stdout:
conf/gateway.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/notify.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/mailer.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/billing.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/auth.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/hooks.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/stats.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/users.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/cache.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/search.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/orders.yaml:2:log_level: debug
conf/worker.yaml:2:log_level: debug

YAML count: 12

stderr:
fatal: not a git repository (or any parent up to mount point /)
Stopping at filesystem boundary (GIT_DISCOVERY_ACROSS_FILESYSTEM not set).

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
files = list(Path('conf').glob('*.yaml')) + list(Path('conf').glob('*.yml'))
assert len(files) == 12, f'expected 12 YAML files, found {len(files)}'
for path in files:
    data = path.read_bytes()
    old = b'log_level: debug'
    assert data.count(old) == 1, f'{path}: expected exactly one target line'
    path.write_bytes(data.replace(old, b'log_level: info'))
PY
python3 verify.py && ./apply-logging.sh

content:
exit_code: 0
stdout:
all 12 configs have log_level: info
